119	// The tab is this view's own filter, not the component's: it selects which
120	// findings exist at all, where a FilterBar query narrows a list that is already
121	// settled. The severity went the other way — it is four cumulative tokens the
122	// table owns (Rule 136), which is what gave `.` back to the sort.
123	func (m *Model) updateFindingsTable() {
124		if m.result == nil {
125			return
126		}
127	
128		m.findingsTable.SetItems(m.filterFindingsByTab())
129		// A change of tab or severity is a change of scope, not a shorter list, so
130		// the cursor goes back to the top and the columns are measured again.
131		// SetItems deliberately does neither on its own.
132		m.findingsTable.GotoTop()
133		m.findingsTable.Remeasure()
134	}
135	
136	// tabCategory maps a tab to the finding category it shows.
137	//
138	// The tabs and scan.Result's counters are now the same classification, applied
139	// once in scan.Categorize: they were two rules that disagreed on three inputs,
140	// each of which produced a finding counted in the header but present in no tab
141	// at all — visible nowhere, which is the worst way for a finding to be wrong.
142	var tabCategory = map[int]scan.Category{
143		TabCVE:       scan.CategoryVulnerability,
144		TabSecrets:   scan.CategorySecret,
145		TabLicense:   scan.CategoryLicense,
146		TabMisconfig: scan.CategoryMisconfiguration,
147		TabCIScore:   scan.CategoryCIScore,
148	}
149	
150	// filterFindingsByTab returns findings filtered by the active tab
151	func (m *Model) filterFindingsByTab() []scan.Finding {
152		if m.result == nil {
153			return nil
154		}
155	
156		want, ok := tabCategory[m.activeTab]
157		if !ok {
158			return nil
159		}
160		var filtered []scan.Finding
161		for _, f := range m.result.Findings {
162			if scan.Categorize(f) == want {
163				filtered = append(filtered, f)
164			}
165		}
166		return filtered
167	}
168	
169	// sourceDisplay returns a display string for the source column.
170	//
171	// Which tool found it, not which category it is — the tab already says the
172	// category, and telling gitleaks from trivy-secret in the Secrets tab is the
173	// point of showing both there.
174	//
175	// A Trivy misconfiguration shows its dialect instead (§3.80): "misconfig"
176	// only repeated the tab's name, while "kubernetes", "helm" or "dockerfile"
177	// is what tells a Deployment's rule from a Dockerfile's on a tab that lists
178	// both — and it is searchable, so `/helm` narrows to the charts. A column of
179	// its own was the alternative, but every other tab would have carried it
180	// empty. A result cached before the dialect was recorded keeps "misconfig".
181	func sourceDisplay(f scan.Finding) string {
182		switch f.Source {
183		case scan.SourceTrivyLicense:
184			return "license"
185		case scan.SourceTrivyMisconfig:
186			if f.IaCType != "" {
187				return f.IaCType
188			}
189			return "misconfig"
190		case scan.SourceKubeconform:
191			// Schema validation, which is what separates it from Trivy's
192			// kubernetes findings on the same manifest.
193			return "schema"
194		case scan.SourceHelm:
195			// Not "helm": that is already the dialect of Trivy's chart findings.
196			return "helm lint"
197		case scan.SourceKustomize:
198			return "kustomize"
199		case scan.SourceBuildContext:
200			// DevDesk's own check (§3.81): what a COPY of the whole context takes
201			// into the image, which no scanner reports.
202			return "context"
203		case scan.SourceGitleaks:
204			return "gitleaks"
205		case scan.SourceTrivySecret:
206			return "trivy"
207		case scan.SourceTrivy:
208			return "vuln"
209		default:
210			return f.Source
211		}
212	}
213	
214	// countFindingsByTab returns the count of findings for each tab. These are the
215	// numbers on the tab labels, and scan.Result's counters are the same ones.
216	func (m *Model) countFindingsByTab() (cve, secrets, licenses, misconfigs, ci int) {
217		if m.result == nil {
218			return 0, 0, 0, 0, 0
219		}
220	
221		for _, f := range m.result.Findings {
222			switch scan.Categorize(f) {
223			case scan.CategoryVulnerability:
224				cve++
225			case scan.CategorySecret:
226				secrets++
227			case scan.CategoryLicense:
228				licenses++
229			case scan.CategoryMisconfiguration:
230				misconfigs++
231			case scan.CategoryCIScore:
232				ci++
233			}
234		}
235		return cve, secrets, licenses, misconfigs, ci
236	}
237	
238	// enterTab is what entering a tab starts: the Dockerfile read of the
239	// Remediation tab, the invalid-setting warning of the Misconfigurations one.
240	func (m *Model) enterTab() tea.Cmd {
241		return tea.Batch(m.enterRemediationTab(), m.enterPSSTab())
242	}
243	
244	// enterRemediationTab reads the Dockerfiles when the tab just switched to is the
245	// Remediation one, and does nothing on any other.
246	func (m *Model) enterRemediationTab() tea.Cmd {
247		if m.activeTab != TabRemediation {
248			return nil
249		}
250		return m.enterRemediation()
251	}
252	
253	// switchTab switches to the given tab index and refreshes the table
254	func (m *Model) switchTab(tab int) {
255		m.activeTab = tab
256		// The Pod Security filter belongs to one visit of the Misconfigurations
257		// tab: it is off on the way in and on the way out.
258		// Only when it is on: switching off an off token rebuilds the rows and
259		// measures the columns again for nothing.
260		if m.findingsTable.IsTokenActive(pssToken) {
261			m.findingsTable.SetTokenActive(pssToken, false)
262		}
263		// The CI tab carries a score line above the table, so the height changes
264		// with the tab and not only with the window.
265		m.resizeFindings()
266		m.footer.Clear()
267		m.updateFindingsTable()
268	}
269	
270	// handleIgnoreSecret prompts confirmation to ignore a secret finding.
271	//
272	// Gitleaks findings only. .gitleaksignore is matched on a Gitleaks fingerprint,
273	// which a Trivy secret does not have — AddToGitleaksIgnore would fabricate one
274	// from the file and rule, write it, and report success for a line Gitleaks will
275	// never match and Trivy never reads. Refusing says so instead.
276	func (m Model) handleIgnoreSecret() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
277		if exclude := m.canExclude(); !exclude.Enabled() {
278			return m, m.footer.Warn(exclude.Reason)
279		}
280		finding, _ := m.findingsTable.Selected()
281		m.findingToIgnore = &finding
282		m.confirmModal = sharedcomponents.NewConfirmModal(
283			"Ignore Secret",
284			fmt.Sprintf("Add this secret to .gitleaksignore?\n\nFile: %s\nRule: %s", finding.File, finding.ID),
285		)
286		return m, nil
287	}
288	
289	// The two findings actions, and why each does not apply (Rule 130).
290	const (
291		reasonNoFinding    = "No finding selected"
292		reasonNotASecret   = "REDACTED"
293		reasonNotGitleaks  = "Only Gitleaks findings can be added to .gitleaksignore"
294		reasonNotCITab     = "The resolved pipeline belongs to the CI tab"
295		reasonNotARepo     = "An image has no pipeline"
296		reasonNoResolution = "This forge does not resolve a pipeline server-side"
297		reasonNothingToSee = "No finding to open"
298	)
299	
300	// canOpenFinding reports whether enter has a row to detail.
301	func (m Model) canOpenFinding() shortcut.Availability {
302		if _, ok := m.findingsTable.Selected(); !ok {
303			return shortcut.Unavailable(reasonNothingToSee)
304		}
305		return shortcut.Availability{}
306	}
307	
308	// canExclude reports whether X applies to the selected finding.
309	//
310	// .gitleaksignore is matched on a Gitleaks fingerprint, which a Trivy secret
311	// does not have — fabricating one would report success for a line nothing will
312	// ever match. The tab is checked first because it is the coarser answer: on
313	// the CVE tab the key means nothing at all, whatever the row.
314	// openPipelineKey opens the pipeline the forge resolves for this repository.
315	//
316	// It is a **declared exception** to the uppercase vocabulary
317	// (keymap.DeclaredExceptions), on the precedent of `c` in oci/network-inspect
318	// and for the reason written there: the action exists on one sub-screen, and
319	// burning one of the three remaining free capitals for it would cost more than
320	// it returns.
321	//
322	// `o` and not `p`: `o` already means "open what this screen points at" in this
323	// view's details state, where it opens a finding's reference. One verb, two
324	// screens, and the shortcut column is replaced by the mode either way.
325	const openPipelineKey = "o"
326	
327	// canOpenPipeline decides whether the resolved pipeline can be fetched.
328	//
329	// The tab is checked first for canExclude's reason — it is the coarser answer,
330	// and off the CI tab the key means nothing whatever the row. The shape is
331	// checked before anything is read: a GitHub context cannot answer this at all,
332	// and finding that out after a keystroke and a git call would be worse than
333	// saying so in the column.
334	func (m Model) canOpenPipeline() shortcut.Availability {
335		switch {
336		case m.activeTab != TabCIScore:
337			return shortcut.Unavailable(reasonNotCITab)
338		case m.result == nil || m.result.TargetType != scan.TargetDirectory:
339			return shortcut.Unavailable(reasonNotARepo)
340		case !forge.ShapeFor(m.config.Forge.Type).MergedCIConfig:
341			return shortcut.Unavailable(reasonNoResolution)
342		}
343		return shortcut.Availability{}
344	}
345	
346	// openResolvedPipeline hands the document to the router, which opens the
347	// viewer on it. The fetch is the source's, so it runs on the viewer's own Cmd
348	// (Rule 110) and its failures are reported where the document would have been.
349	func (m Model) openResolvedPipeline() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
350		// The refusal is never silent (Rule 130), and it is a Warn rather than an
351		// Error: nothing failed, the key does not apply as asked (Rule 128). The
352		// reason is the one canOpenPipeline computed, so the footer and the greyed
353		// entry cannot be about different things.
354		if a := m.canOpenPipeline(); !a.Enabled() {
355			return m, m.footer.Warn(a.Reason)
356		}
357		source := pipelineSource{
358			RepoPath: m.result.Target,
359			Label:    theme.FoldHome(m.result.Target),
360			Forge:    m.config.Forge,
361			Secrets:  m.secrets,
362			Findings: m.result.Findings,
363		}
364		return m, func() tea.Msg { return uiviewer.OpenRequestMsg{Source: source} }
365	}
366	
367	func (m Model) canExclude() shortcut.Availability {
368		if m.activeTab != TabSecrets {
369			return shortcut.Unavailable(reasonNotASecret)
370		}
371		finding, ok := m.findingsTable.Selected()
372		switch {
373		case !ok:
374			return shortcut.Unavailable(reasonNoFinding)
375		case finding.Source != scan.SourceGitleaks:
376			return shortcut.Unavailable(reasonNotGitleaks)
377		}
378		return shortcut.Availability{}
379	}
380	
381	// handleResultsState processes input in results state.
382	//
383	// The search answers first, and every key below is unreachable while it has the
384	// keyboard: "c" is a character in a query, "esc" cancels the search rather than
385	// leaving the results, and "enter" confirms it rather than opening a finding.
386	// The inventory has had this guard since it gained a bar; this state gained one
387	// the day the severity floor became tokens, and never got the guard with it.
388	func (m Model) handleResultsState(msg tea.KeyPressMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
389		if m.findingsTable.InEditMode() {
390			return m, m.findingsTable.Update(msg)
391		}
392		if m.activeTab == TabRemediation {
393			if next, cmd, handled := m.handleRemediationKey(msg); handled {
394				return next, cmd
395			}
396		}
397		switch msg.String() {
398		case "esc":
399			// No origin view means this view was opened directly, so esc stays
400			// inside it and goes back to whichever landing state it opened on.
401			if m.OriginView == "" {
402				return m.goHome()
403			}
404			return m, func() tea.Msg { return BackToOriginMsg{Origin: m.OriginView} }
405		case "enter":
406			if finding, ok := m.findingsTable.Selected(); ok {
407				// The details view is about a finding, not about a row index — an
408				// index would name a different one the moment the list changed
409				// under it, which is how workspaces got D24.
410				m.selectedFinding = &finding
411				m.state = StateDetails
412				m.detailsViewport.SetWidth(m.width)
413				m.detailsViewport.SetHeight(m.height)
414				m.detailsViewport.SetContent(m.buildDetailsContent())
415				m.detailsViewport.GotoTop()
416			}
417			return m, nil
418		case "ctrl+r":
419			m.activeTab = TabCVE
420			return m.goHome()
421		case "tab":
422			m.switchTab((m.activeTab + 1) % tabCount)
423			cmd := m.enterTab()
424			return m, cmd
425		case "shift+tab":
426			m.switchTab((m.activeTab + tabCount - 1) % tabCount)
427			cmd := m.enterTab()
428			return m, cmd
429		// 1-4 jumped straight to a tab. They were the application's only numeric
430		// bindings, and an exception in a single view is precisely what §3.26
431		// dismantles — tab reaches all four.
432		case "c", "h", "m", "l":
433			return m.toggleSeverity(msg.String())
434		case pssFilterKey:
435			return m.togglePSS()
436		case keymap.Exclude:
437			return m.handleIgnoreSecret()
438		case openPipelineKey:
439			return m.openResolvedPipeline()
440		case keymap.Scan:
441			// Off the Remediation tab this refuses, with the reason (Rule 130).
442			return m.scanCandidates()
443		case writeRemediationKey:
444			// One key, one verb — write the file — applied to whichever tab's
445			// object. The Remediation tab writes a base image, the
446			// Misconfigurations tab a built-in fix; anywhere else the refusal says
447			// which tab it belongs to (Rule 130).
448			if m.activeTab == TabMisconfig {
449				return m.prepareMisconfigFix()
450			}
451			return m.prepareRemediationWrite()
452		}
453		// `.` is the sort again, and the search and the severity tokens are the
454		// table's (Rule 136).
455		return m, m.findingsTable.Update(msg)
456	}
457	
458	// toggleSeverity flips one severity token. Cumulative: c and h together ask for
459	// "CRITICAL or HIGH", which is the question a threshold cycle could not put.
460	func (m Model) toggleSeverity(key string) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
461		label := map[string]string{"c": "critical", "h": "high", "m": "medium", "l": "low"}[key]
462		m.findingsTable.SetTokenActive(label, !m.findingsTable.IsTokenActive(label))
463		m.findingsTable.GotoTop()
464		return m, nil
465	}
466	
467	// resizeFindings lays the findings table out. Every tab gets the whole height:
468	// the CI tab used to give two rows to a score line above the table, and losing
469	// two findings on one tab out of five — for a letter the inventory already
470	// carries per target — was not worth the jump on every tab switch.
471	func (m *Model) resizeFindings() {
472		m.findingsTable.Resize(m.width, max(m.height, 5))
473		m.remediation.table.Resize(m.width, max(m.height, 5))
474	}

4		"fmt"
5

14		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/keymap"
15		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/shortcut"

17		uiviewer "github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/viewer"
18	)
19	
20	// findingColumns describes the findings table.
21	//
22	// The table opens on the order the scanner reported — `SortColumn: -1`, which
23	// datatable keeps as a stop on the cycle, so `.` always leads back to it. Every
24	// column sorts, because `.` was handed back to the sort when the severity floor
25	// became four tokens (§3.26) and then no column was ever given a `Less`:
26	// CycleSort returned on its first line and the header advertised a key that did
27	// nothing at all.
28	//
29	// Three columns search, and that is not optional either. Declaring tokens makes
30	// `Searchable()` true, so `/` already opened a query — against no searchable
31	// column, which matches nothing and empties the table. The bar's own left half
32	// says `/ search...` whether or not anything answers it.
33	//
34	// Severity searches nothing on purpose: c/h/m/l are the severity filter, and a
35	// second way to ask one question is what this codebase spends its time
36	// removing. The Title is not pre-truncated either — bubbles cuts every cell to
37	// its column width with the same ellipsis, and doing it by hand at width-3
38	// first only cost three characters of title.
39	func findingColumns() []datatable.Column[scan.Finding] {
40		return []datatable.Column[scan.Finding]{
41			{
42				Title: "Severity", Sizing: datatable.SizingFixed, MinWidth: 10,
43				Cell: func(f scan.Finding) string { return string(f.Severity) },
44				// The same palette the selected row uses, so a severity reads the
45				// same colour whether or not the cursor is on it.
46				Style: func(f scan.Finding) lipgloss.Style { return theme.SeverityTextStyle(string(f.Severity)) },
47				Less:  func(a, b scan.Finding) bool { return severityRank(a.Severity) < severityRank(b.Severity) },
48			},
49			{
50				Title: "ID", Sizing: datatable.SizingContent, MinWidth: 18,
51				Cell:   func(f scan.Finding) string { return f.ID },
52				Less:   func(a, b scan.Finding) bool { return a.ID < b.ID },
53				Search: func(f scan.Finding) string { return f.ID },
54			},
55			{
56				Title: "Title", Sizing: datatable.SizingContent, MinWidth: 20, Flex: 1,
57				// The Pod Security label is a prefix of the text (DEVDESK-686); the
58				// sort stays on the title and the search sees the label.
59				Cell:   titleWithLabel,
60				Less:   func(a, b scan.Finding) bool { return a.Title < b.Title },
61				Search: func(f scan.Finding) string { return titleWithLabel(f) + " " + f.PkgName + " " + f.File },
62			},
63			{
64				Title: "Source", Sizing: datatable.SizingFixed, Optional: true, MinWidth: 14,
65				Cell:   sourceDisplay,
66				Less:   func(a, b scan.Finding) bool { return sourceDisplay(a) < sourceDisplay(b) },
67				Search: sourceDisplay,
68			},
69		}
70	}
71	
72	// severityRank orders the levels by how bad they are, which is the only order
73	// worth sorting this column by: alphabetically, CRITICAL lands between no two
74	// levels it belongs with — HIGH, LOW, MEDIUM — so a descending sort would put
75	// MEDIUM at the top and bury the finding the user opened the view for.
76	//
77	// Ascending is least-severe-first, so `.`'s second press (descending, Rule 111)
78	// is the one that answers "what is worst here".
79	//
80	// UNKNOWN ranks below LOW rather than above CRITICAL: it is what a scanner
81	// says when it has no score, not a claim that something is worse than critical.
82	// It has no token either, for the same reason — see severityToken.
83	func severityRank(s scan.SeverityLevel) int {
84		switch s {
85		case scan.SeverityCritical:
86			return 4
87		case scan.SeverityHigh:
88			return 3
89		case scan.SeverityMedium:
90			return 2
91		case scan.SeverityLow:
92			return 1
93		default:
94			return 0
95		}
96	}
97	
98	// findingSelectedStyles colours the selected row by the severity under the
99	// cursor. It is what refreshSelectionStyle did, minus its own bounds check.
100	func findingSelectedStyles(f scan.Finding) table.Styles {
101		return theme.TableStylesForSeverity(string(f.Severity))
102	}
103	
104	// Tab constants for results view
105	const (
106		TabCVE       = 0
107		TabSecrets   = 1
108		TabLicense   = 2
109		TabMisconfig = 3
110		TabCIScore   = 4
111		// TabRemediation is not a category of finding: it has no entry in
112		// tabCategory and its body is its own table (remediation.go).
113		TabRemediation = 5
114		tabCount       = 6
115	)
116	
117	// updateFindingsTable populates the findings table based on active tab and filters.
118	//
119	// The tab is this view's own filter, not the component's: it selects which
120	// findings exist at all, where a FilterBar query narrows a list that is already
121	// settled. The severity went the other way — it is four cumulative tokens the
122	// table owns (Rule 136), which is what gave `.` back to the sort.
123	func (m *Model) updateFindingsTable() {
124		if m.result == nil {
125			return
126		}
127	
128		m.findingsTable.SetItems(m.filterFindingsByTab())
129		// A change of tab or severity is a change of scope, not a shorter list, so
130		// the cursor goes back to the top and the columns are measured again.
131		// SetItems deliberately does neither on its own.
132		m.findingsTable.GotoTop()
133		m.findingsTable.Remeasure()
134	}
135	
136	// tabCategory maps a tab to the finding category it shows.
137	//
138	// The tabs and scan.Result's counters are now the same classification, applied
139	// once in scan.Categorize: they were two rules that disagreed on three inputs,
140	// each of which produced a finding counted in the header but present in no tab
141	// at all — visible nowhere, which is the worst way for a finding to be wrong.
142	var tabCategory = map[int]scan.Category{
143		TabCVE:       scan.CategoryVulnerability,
144		TabSecrets:   scan.CategorySecret,
145		TabLicense:   scan.CategoryLicense,
146		TabMisconfig: scan.CategoryMisconfiguration,
147		TabCIScore:   scan.CategoryCIScore,
148	}
149	
150	// filterFindingsByTab returns findings filtered by the active tab
151	func (m *Model) filterFindingsByTab() []scan.Finding {
152		if m.result == nil {
153			return nil
154		}
155	
156		want, ok := tabCategory[m.activeTab]
157		if !ok {
158			return nil
159		}
160		var filtered []scan.Finding
161		for _, f := range m.result.Findings {
162			if scan.Categorize(f) == want {
163				filtered = append(filtered, f)
164			}
165		}
166		return filtered
167	}

169	// sourceDisplay returns a display string for the source column.
170	//
171	// Which tool found it, not which category it is — the tab already says the
172	// category, and telling gitleaks from trivy-secret in the Secrets tab is the
173	// point of showing both there.
174	//
175	// A Trivy misconfiguration shows its dialect instead (§3.80): "misconfig"
176	// only repeated the tab's name, while "kubernetes", "helm" or "dockerfile"
177	// is what tells a Deployment's rule from a Dockerfile's on a tab that lists
178	// both — and it is searchable, so `/helm` narrows to the charts. A column of
179	// its own was the alternative, but every other tab would have carried it
180	// empty. A result cached before the dialect was recorded keeps "misconfig".
181	func sourceDisplay(f scan.Finding) string {
182		switch f.Source {
183		case scan.SourceTrivyLicense:
184			return "license"
185		case scan.SourceTrivyMisconfig:
186			if f.IaCType != "" {
187				return f.IaCType
188			}
189			return "misconfig"
190		case scan.SourceKubeconform:
191			// Schema validation, which is what separates it from Trivy's
192			// kubernetes findings on the same manifest.
193			return "schema"
194		case scan.SourceHelm:
195			// Not "helm": that is already the dialect of Trivy's chart findings.
196			return "helm lint"
197		case scan.SourceKustomize:
198			return "kustomize"
199		case scan.SourceBuildContext:
200			// DevDesk's own check (§3.81): what a COPY of the whole context takes
201			// into the image, which no scanner reports.
202			return "context"
203		case scan.SourceGitleaks:
204			return "gitleaks"
205		case scan.SourceTrivySecret:
206			return "trivy"
207		case scan.SourceTrivy:
208			return "vuln"
209		default:
210			return f.Source
211		}
212	}

214	// countFindingsByTab returns the count of findings for each tab. These are the
215	// numbers on the tab labels, and scan.Result's counters are the same ones.
216	func (m *Model) countFindingsByTab() (cve, secrets, licenses, misconfigs, ci int) {
217		if m.result == nil {
218			return 0, 0, 0, 0, 0
219		}
220	
221		for _, f := range m.result.Findings {
222			switch scan.Categorize(f) {
223			case scan.CategoryVulnerability:
224				cve++
225			case scan.CategorySecret:
226				secrets++
227			case scan.CategoryLicense:
228				licenses++
229			case scan.CategoryMisconfiguration:
230				misconfigs++
231			case scan.CategoryCIScore:
232				ci++
233			}
234		}
235		return cve, secrets, licenses, misconfigs, ci
236	}

245	// Remediation one, and does nothing on any other.

248			return nil

253	// switchTab switches to the given tab index and refreshes the table
254	func (m *Model) switchTab(tab int) {
255		m.activeTab = tab
256		// The Pod Security filter belongs to one visit of the Misconfigurations
257		// tab: it is off on the way in and on the way out.
258		// Only when it is on: switching off an off token rebuilds the rows and
259		// measures the columns again for nothing.
260		if m.findingsTable.IsTokenActive(pssToken) {
261			m.findingsTable.SetTokenActive(pssToken, false)
262		}
263		// The CI tab carries a score line above the table, so the height changes
264		// with the tab and not only with the window.
265		m.resizeFindings()
266		m.footer.Clear()
267		m.updateFindingsTable()

270	// handleIgnoreSecret prompts confirmation to ignore a secret finding.
271	//
272	// Gitleaks findings only. .gitleaksignore is matched on a Gitleaks fingerprint,
273	// which a Trivy secret does not have — AddToGitleaksIgnore would fabricate one
274	// from the file and rule, write it, and report success for a line Gitleaks will
275	// never match and Trivy never reads. Refusing says so instead.
276	func (m Model) handleIgnoreSecret() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
277		if exclude := m.canExclude(); !exclude.Enabled() {
278			return m, m.footer.Warn(exclude.Reason)
279		}
280		finding, _ := m.findingsTable.Selected()
281		m.findingToIgnore = &finding
282		m.confirmModal = sharedcomponents.NewConfirmModal(
283			"Ignore Secret",
284			fmt.Sprintf("Add this secret to .gitleaksignore?\n\nFile: %s\nRule: %s", finding.File, finding.ID),
285		)
286		return m, nil
287	}

289	// The two findings actions, and why each does not apply (Rule 130).
290	const (
291		reasonNoFinding    = "No finding selected"
292		reasonNotASecret   = "REDACTED"
293		reasonNotGitleaks  = "Only Gitleaks findings can be added to .gitleaksignore"
294		reasonNotCITab     = "The resolved pipeline belongs to the CI tab"
295		reasonNotARepo     = "An image has no pipeline"
296		reasonNoResolution = "This forge does not resolve a pipeline server-side"
297		reasonNothingToSee = "No finding to open"
298	)
299	
300	// canOpenFinding reports whether enter has a row to detail.
301	func (m Model) canOpenFinding() shortcut.Availability {
302		if _, ok := m.findingsTable.Selected(); !ok {
303			return shortcut.Unavailable(reasonNothingToSee)
304		}
305		return shortcut.Availability{}
306	}
307	
308	// canExclude reports whether X applies to the selected finding.
309	//
310	// .gitleaksignore is matched on a Gitleaks fingerprint, which a Trivy secret
311	// does not have — fabricating one would report success for a line nothing will
312	// ever match. The tab is checked first because it is the coarser answer: on
313	// the CVE tab the key means nothing at all, whatever the row.
314	// openPipelineKey opens the pipeline the forge resolves for this repository.
315	//
316	// It is a **declared exception** to the uppercase vocabulary
317	// (keymap.DeclaredExceptions), on the precedent of `c` in oci/network-inspect
318	// and for the reason written there: the action exists on one sub-screen, and
319	// burning one of the three remaining free capitals for it would cost more than
320	// it returns.
321	//
322	// `o` and not `p`: `o` already means "open what this screen points at" in this
323	// view's details state, where it opens a finding's reference. One verb, two
324	// screens, and the shortcut column is replaced by the mode either way.
325	const openPipelineKey = "o"
326	
327	// canOpenPipeline decides whether the resolved pipeline can be fetched.
328	//
329	// The tab is checked first for canExclude's reason — it is the coarser answer,
330	// and off the CI tab the key means nothing whatever the row. The shape is
331	// checked before anything is read: a GitHub context cannot answer this at all,
332	// and finding that out after a keystroke and a git call would be worse than
333	// saying so in the column.
334	func (m Model) canOpenPipeline() shortcut.Availability {
335		switch {
336		case m.activeTab != TabCIScore:
337			return shortcut.Unavailable(reasonNotCITab)
338		case m.result == nil || m.result.TargetType != scan.TargetDirectory:
339			return shortcut.Unavailable(reasonNotARepo)
340		case !forge.ShapeFor(m.config.Forge.Type).MergedCIConfig:
341			return shortcut.Unavailable(reasonNoResolution)
342		}
343		return shortcut.Availability{}
344	}
345	
346	// openResolvedPipeline hands the document to the router, which opens the
347	// viewer on it. The fetch is the source's, so it runs on the viewer's own Cmd
348	// (Rule 110) and its failures are reported where the document would have been.
349	func (m Model) openResolvedPipeline() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
350		// The refusal is never silent (Rule 130), and it is a Warn rather than an
351		// Error: nothing failed, the key does not apply as asked (Rule 128). The
352		// reason is the one canOpenPipeline computed, so the footer and the greyed
353		// entry cannot be about different things.
354		if a := m.canOpenPipeline(); !a.Enabled() {
355			return m, m.footer.Warn(a.Reason)
356		}
357		source := pipelineSource{
358			RepoPath: m.result.Target,
359			Label:    theme.FoldHome(m.result.Target),
360			Forge:    m.config.Forge,
361			Secrets:  m.secrets,
362			Findings: m.result.Findings,
363		}
364		return m, func() tea.Msg { return uiviewer.OpenRequestMsg{Source: source} }
365	}
366	
367	func (m Model) canExclude() shortcut.Availability {
368		if m.activeTab != TabSecrets {
369			return shortcut.Unavailable(reasonNotASecret)
370		}
371		finding, ok := m.findingsTable.Selected()
372		switch {
373		case !ok:
374			return shortcut.Unavailable(reasonNoFinding)
375		case finding.Source != scan.SourceGitleaks:
376			return shortcut.Unavailable(reasonNotGitleaks)
377		}
378		return shortcut.Availability{}
379	}

381	// handleResultsState processes input in results state.
382	//
383	// The search answers first, and every key below is unreachable while it has the
384	// keyboard: "c" is a character in a query, "esc" cancels the search rather than
385	// leaving the results, and "enter" confirms it rather than opening a finding.
386	// The inventory has had this guard since it gained a bar; this state gained one
387	// the day the severity floor became tokens, and never got the guard with it.
388	func (m Model) handleResultsState(msg tea.KeyPressMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
389		if m.findingsTable.InEditMode() {
390			return m, m.findingsTable.Update(msg)
391		}
392		if m.activeTab == TabRemediation {
393			if next, cmd, handled := m.handleRemediationKey(msg); handled {
394				return next, cmd
395			}
396		}
397		switch msg.String() {
398		case "esc":
399			// No origin view means this view was opened directly, so esc stays
400			// inside it and goes back to whichever landing state it opened on.
401			if m.OriginView == "" {
402				return m.goHome()
403			}
404			return m, func() tea.Msg { return BackToOriginMsg{Origin: m.OriginView} }
405		case "enter":
406			if finding, ok := m.findingsTable.Selected(); ok {
407				// The details view is about a finding, not about a row index — an
408				// index would name a different one the moment the list changed
409				// under it, which is how workspaces got D24.
410				m.selectedFinding = &finding
411				m.state = StateDetails
412				m.detailsViewport.SetWidth(m.width)
413				m.detailsViewport.SetHeight(m.height)
414				m.detailsViewport.SetContent(m.buildDetailsContent())
415				m.detailsViewport.GotoTop()
416			}
417			return m, nil
418		case "ctrl+r":
419			m.activeTab = TabCVE
420			return m.goHome()
421		case "tab":
422			m.switchTab((m.activeTab + 1) % tabCount)
423			cmd := m.enterTab()
424			return m, cmd
425		case "shift+tab":
426			m.switchTab((m.activeTab + tabCount - 1) % tabCount)
427			cmd := m.enterTab()
428			return m, cmd
429		// 1-4 jumped straight to a tab. They were the application's only numeric
430		// bindings, and an exception in a single view is precisely what §3.26
431		// dismantles — tab reaches all four.
432		case "c", "h", "m", "l":
433			return m.toggleSeverity(msg.String())
434		case pssFilterKey:
435			return m.togglePSS()
436		case keymap.Exclude:
437			return m.handleIgnoreSecret()
438		case openPipelineKey:
439			return m.openResolvedPipeline()
440		case keymap.Scan:
441			// Off the Remediation tab this refuses, with the reason (Rule 130).
442			return m.scanCandidates()
443		case writeRemediationKey:
444			// One key, one verb — write the file — applied to whichever tab's
445			// object. The Remediation tab writes a base image, the
446			// Misconfigurations tab a built-in fix; anywhere else the refusal says
447			// which tab it belongs to (Rule 130).
448			if m.activeTab == TabMisconfig {
449				return m.prepareMisconfigFix()
450			}
451			return m.prepareRemediationWrite()
452		}
453		// `.` is the sort again, and the search and the severity tokens are the
454		// table's (Rule 136).
455		return m, m.findingsTable.Update(msg)
456	}
457	
458	// toggleSeverity flips one severity token. Cumulative: c and h together ask for
459	// "CRITICAL or HIGH", which is the question a threshold cycle could not put.
460	func (m Model) toggleSeverity(key string) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
461		label := map[string]string{"c": "critical", "h": "high", "m": "medium", "l": "low"}[key]
462		m.findingsTable.SetTokenActive(label, !m.findingsTable.IsTokenActive(label))
463		m.findingsTable.GotoTop()
464		return m, nil
465	}
466	
467	// resizeFindings lays the findings table out. Every tab gets the whole height:
468	// the CI tab used to give two rows to a score line above the table, and losing
469	// two findings on one tab out of five — for a letter the inventory already
470	// carries per target — was not worth the jump on every tab switch.
471	func (m *Model) resizeFindings() {
472		m.findingsTable.Resize(m.width, max(m.height, 5))
473		m.remediation.table.Resize(m.width, max(m.height, 5))
474	}
